turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell inquired with a raised eyebrow whether Mr Worthing was suggesting that his residence was not his own property.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack assured Lady Bracknell that it was his own property, though he had inherited it from his uncle, whom he had never met.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell inquired whether Mr Worthing had a clear title to the property and if he could produce a legal deed to prove it.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack explained to Lady Bracknell that he had inherited the property and the legal documents were in his possession, though he had not yet had the chance to look at them thoroughly.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell pressed on, her tone sharp and inquiring, whether Mr Worthing could produce the legal deed forthwith to substantiate his claim.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen rolled her eyes at her mother’s relentless questioning, muttering under her breath that everything must be so tedious.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell leaned forward, her eyes narrowing. She pressed on, her tone sharp and inquiring, whether Mr Worthing could produce the legal deed forthwith to substantiate his claim.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack explained to Lady Bracknell, with a slight nod, that he would be happy to produce the deed as soon as possible, though it would require some time to locate it.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell raised an eyebrow, her expression unchanged. She inquired with a hint of impatience whether Mr Worthing could provide a more immediate solution to this matter, for time was of the essence in such affairs.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen sighed loudly, rolling her eyes again, telling her mother that if the matter was so urgent, why could not Jack be given a bit more time? It was not as if he was trying to deceive anyone.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell fixed Gwendolen with a stern gaze, her voice dripping with impatience, telling her daughter that such matters were not to be trifled with and that she must understand the importance of immediate action in securing one’s position in society.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell turned her gaze back to Jack, her voice firm and unyielding, stating that she expected more punctuality and preparedness from someone of his standing.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack, feeling somewhat flustered, assured Lady Bracknell that he was indeed making every effort to meet her expectations and would do his utmost to rectify the situation as soon as possible.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell gave Jack a piercing look, her voice cold and unyielding, stating that she was not interested in empty promises and that Jack must present a concrete plan of action at once.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack nodded, his expression earnest, telling Lady Bracknell that he understood the gravity of the situation and would present a detailed plan that evening.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She fixed Jack with a stern look, her voice cold and sharp, telling him that she expected tangible results, not vague assurances.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack understood Lady Bracknell’s concerns and promised to present a detailed proposal that evening, one that would satisfy her requirements.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She gave a sharp nod, her eyes narrowing slightly. She told Jack that she would await his proposal with interest and that it must be both practical and convincing.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack nodded again, assuring Lady Bracknell that he would work tirelessly to meet her expectations.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She dismissed Jack with a curt nod, her tone leaving no room for further discussion. She would expect nothing less than perfection from him, as she did from all those under her patronage.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell that she was engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that she was not engaged to anyone and that when she did become engaged, she or her father would inform her of the fact.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell, 'Mamma!'

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to go to the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to get into the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack to take a seat.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he preferred standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she felt bound to inform him that he was not down on her list of eligible young men.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he must admit he smoked.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was glad to hear it and that a man should always have an occupation of some kind.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he was twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he knew everything or nothing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he knew nothing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was pleased to hear it and that she did not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if his income was in land or in investments.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was in investments.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that it was satisfactory.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he had a country house with some land attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that a country house was satisfactory and asked how many bedrooms it had.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he owned a house in Belgrave Square, but it was let by the year to Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she did not know Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that Lady Bloxham went about very little and was a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that nowadays that was no guarantee of respectability of character and asked what number in Belgrave Square.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that the number was 149.
